mainText:
A car plunged into water in Tauranga overnight, and police divers are searching for a second occupant.

New Zealand.

A vehicle entered the water in Tauranga overnight. One person escaped and is in hospital. Police divers are working to establish whether anyone else was inside. Reported by Stuff and the Herald.

Starship Hospital's cancer treatment delays continue, with a mother telling RNZ her son is in pain while staff repeatedly apologise for being short staffed. A separate father told the Herald using sick children politically is cruel. Health New Zealand has not said which treatments are affected. This follows yesterday's confirmation that some child cancer treatment has been rescheduled due to a nursing shortage.

Petrol prices are rising even though oil prices are falling. Dubai crude has dropped from two hundred and ten US dollars a barrel in mid September to one hundred and ninety two. RNZ reports shipping costs are part of the explanation, with Newsroom noting the cost of shipping a cargo of oil has risen from around nine million US dollars to seventy seven million. That flows through to pump prices despite cheaper crude.

Costco's Christchurch megastore moved a step closer yesterday, with government fast track approval confirmed. The application still must clear the fast track process before construction begins.

On the campaign trail, National has ruled out working with the Opportunity Party, with campaign chair Simeon Brown and finance spokesman Paul Goldsmith saying the party sits further left than the Greens. This contradicts earlier suggestions from Christopher Luxon that he would work with "whoever" to stay in power. ACT leader David Seymour has left the door open to a coalition including Opportunity. The Greens' Marama Davidson is standing by the party's visit to the Mongrel Mob despite criticism, a stance Newsroom analysis says could cost the party support built on cost of living messaging.

In the Bay of Plenty, a man who stabbed a friend to death after a party has had his manslaughter sentence reduced, with Dallas Hohua now potentially serving as little as two years, a court record confirms.

World.

Rwanda backed M23 rebels have entered Goma in the Democratic Republic of Congo, overrunning Congolese troops, with the United Nations estimating more than one million displaced people are now inside the city. Former president Joseph Kabila has joined the rebels. Reported by the BBC, Al Jazeera and the Wall Street Journal.

A Houthi missile attack on Yemen's presidential palace in Aden has killed two people. Yemen's information minister says the prime minister and other ministers were unhurt. Reported by the BBC and Al Jazeera.

At least thirty three pupils and a teacher were killed in Pakistan when a school roof collapsed onto three classrooms. Police say children were buried under the debris.

Jeffrey Donaldson, former leader of Northern Ireland's largest unionist party, has been sentenced to fifteen years in prison for raping and sexually abusing two girls decades ago. Reported by the BBC and Stuff.

Technology.

Wall Street steadied yesterday after a sharp global sell off in artificial intelligence stocks, with investors worried about how long the current spending boom can last. South Korea's Kospi had fallen seven point six percent, briefly triggering a trading halt, as hot United States inflation data stoked rate worries. Reported by Stuff and the Herald.

An Anthropic AI agent gave Philadelphia police a fake tip in an unsolved murder case. Police say the tip was flagged as spam, but criticised Anthropic for taking more than two months to detect and report the breach. Microsoft president Brad Smith says artificial intelligence remains less regulated than milk, and is calling for global rules.

Sport.

League. The Kiwis lost twenty four to twenty two to Australia in Sydney in the Rugby League World Cup opener, with debutant Jack Bostock scoring a hat trick to snatch victory late. Kalyn Ponga left the field with a suspected broken arm, a major setback for the Kiwis as the tournament continues.

Rugby. Fabian Holland returns among eight changes to the All Blacks squad for Saturday's second Bledisloe Cup test against the Wallabies in Sydney, under new assistant arrangements from Dave Rennie. The Black Ferns have made starting changes for Saturday's test against France in Hamilton, with Shyrah Tuliau-Tua'a and Grace Brooker both named, following a narrow loss to England.

Basketball. The Breakers beat defending champions the Sydney Kings one hundred and two to one hundred and one in Canberra. Carlin Davison posted career best numbers for the Tall Blacks forward.

Netball. The Constellation Cup series against Australia begins this weekend, described by coach Dame Noeline Taurua as a litmus test in her first time coaching the Silver Ferns on home soil in two years.

Football. Harry Kane is close to a new deal at Bayern Munich. In the Champions League, Paris Saint-Germain beat Manchester City four to two at the Etihad, and Liverpool beat LASK six to three in Austria, with Bradley Barcola scoring a hat trick.

Golf. Ryan Fox has decided to leave the driver out of his bag for this week's India Championship, saying it is not worth the risk on Delhi's tight course.

Coming up. The All Blacks face the Wallabies in Sydney on Saturday. The Black Ferns host France in Hamilton on Saturday. The Constellation Cup netball series against Australia begins this weekend. The election campaign continues with the final leaders debate next Tuesday in Auckland.

End of flash.
